The **Grammy Award for Album of the Year** is an award presented by the [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy") of the United States to "honor artistic achievement, technical proficiency and overall excellence in the recording industry, without regard to album sales, chart position, or critical reception."[[1]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-Overview-1) Commonly known as "**The Big Award**", Album of the Year is the most prestigious award category at the [Grammy Awards](Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), and is one of the four general field categories alongside [Best New Artist](Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist"), [Record of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Song of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") that have been presented annually since the [1st Annual Grammy Awards](1st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "1st Annual Grammy Awards") in 1959.

American [singer-songwriters](Singer-songwriter "Singer-songwriter") [Frank Sinatra](Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra"), [Stevie Wonder](Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder"), [Paul Simon](Paul_Simon "Paul Simon") and [Taylor Swift](Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") have each won Album of the Year award three times, more than any other nominee. Sinatra became the first nominee to win the award in back-to-back years, Wonder is known for winning the award three times in four years, and Swift is the only woman to win the award three times.

The latest winner of the award is *[Harry's House](Harry's_House "Harry's House")* (2022) by English singer [Harry Styles](Harry_Styles "Harry Styles") at the [65th Annual Grammy Awards](65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards").

## Credit rules

Over the years, the rules on who was presented with an award have changed:

- 1959–1965: Artist only.
- 1966–1998: Artist and producer.
- 1999–2002: Artist, producer, and recording engineer or mixer.
- 2003–2017: Artist, featured artist, producer, mastering engineer, and recording engineer or mixer.
- 2018–2020: Artist, producer, songwriter (of new material), mastering engineer, and recording engineer or mixer (only those who were credited on at least 33% playing time of the album)
- 2021–2023: Artist, featured artist/s, producer, songwriter (of new material), mastering engineer and recording engineer or mixer. (regardless of credited playing time)
- 2024–present: Artist, featured artist/s producer, songwriter (of new material), mastering engineer, and recording engineer or mixer (only those who were credited on at least 20% playing time of the album)


The category expanded to include eight nominees in [2019](61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards")[[2]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-2) and to ten in [2022](64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards").[[3]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-3) Beginning with the [2024 ceremony](66th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "66th Annual Grammy Awards"), the number of nominees has been reduced back to eight.[[4]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-4)

Album of the Year is awarded for a whole album, and the award is presented to the artist, featured artist, songwriter, producer, recording engineer, and mastering engineer with significant contributions to that album. The similarly titled Record of the Year is awarded for a single or for one track from an album. This award goes to the performing artist, the producer, recording engineer and/or mixer for that song. ## Process

From 1995 to 2021, members of the [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences") nominated their choices for album of the year. A list of the top twenty records was given to the Nominations Review Committee, a specially selected group of anonymous members, who then selected the top five records to gain a nomination in the category in a special ballot.[[9]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-9) The rest of the members then voted on a winner from the five nominees.[[10]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-10) In 2018, it was announced the number of nominated albums would be increased to eight.[[11]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-11) In 2021, it was announced that the Nomination Review Committees would be disbanded, and the final nominees for album of the year would be decided by votes from members.[[12]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-12) Starting in 2022, the number of nominees in the category increased to 10.[[13]](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year#cite_note-13)

Inspired by 1980s [synth-pop](Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), Swift conceived *1989* to recalibrate her artistry to [pop](Pop_music "Pop music") after critics disputed her status as a [country](Country_music "Country music") musician when she released her fourth studio album, the cross-genre [*Red*](Red_(Taylor_Swift_album) "Red (Taylor Swift album)") (2012), to [country radio](Country_radio "Country radio"). She titled *1989* after her birth year to signify a symbolic artistic rebirth and enlisted [Max Martin](Max_Martin "Max Martin"), who produced *Red*'s [electronic](Electronic_music "Electronic music")-influenced pop tracks, as co-executive producer.

Swift recorded *1989* at studios across the United States, the United Kingdom, and Sweden with an ensemble including Martin, [Shellback](Shellback_(record_producer) "Shellback (record producer)"), [Jack Antonoff](Jack_Antonoff "Jack Antonoff"), [Ryan Tedder](Ryan_Tedder "Ryan Tedder"), [Nathan Chapman](Nathan_Chapman_(record_producer) "Nathan Chapman (record producer)"), and [Imogen Heap](Imogen_Heap "Imogen Heap"). The synth-pop production is characterized by pulsing [synthesizers](Synthesizer "Synthesizer"), [programmed drums](Drum_machine "Drum machine"), and processed backing vocals, a stark contrast to the [acoustic](Acoustic_music "Acoustic music") arrangements of Swift's past albums. Expanding on her autobiographical songwriting, the tracks explore failed romance from a lighthearted perspective and departs from the hostile attitude of her previous songs.

functions.name: fork
functions.desc: Delegate a subtask to a helper agent. Use join(id) to get a helper's result.         You can call this multiple times to take multiple actions. Do not delegate the entire task you were given.         If the user's query can be resolved in parallel, call this multiple times then use join("all").
